chung.Description: This course provides core theories in multimedia production to prepare students for media production practice. It covers the entire media production process, from brainstorming ideas and content preparation to production execution. The scope of production varies from podcasts, webcasts, TVCs, promotional videos (promos), teasers, and trailers to movies and more. The course aims to help students practice with small-scale projects to become familiar with the techniques and the overall workflow.
chung.StudentTasks:
1. Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination

2. Actively participate in class activities

3. Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class

4. Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose

5. Read the textbook in advance

6. Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn/) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

7. Complete course's Portfolio with full contents of exercises and submit to the teacher after the course with references including AI sources

danhGia: Practice brainstorming a story. Students choose an idea and develop it into a short story.

AI-Assisted Idea Generation & Structuring

Students are permitted to use AI to brainstorm ideas or provide ideas on structuring of documents. They cannot create content using AI. Students should provide AI prompts used and drafts of their work and acknowledge how they used AI in their final submission.

- From session 1 to 7
- Each student chooses an idea and develops it into a short story (half A4 page), then writes a script.
- Students are recommended to use AI tools for brainstorming and generating reference ideas.
Group work to film a short video following the shot list.

AI-Assisted Editing

Students are permitted to use AI to edit their work and make improvements to the clarity and quality of their work. AI can be used, but original work with no AI content and AI prompts and responses must be provided in appendix. Student acknowledge how they used AI in their final submission.

From session 10 to 21
Each group (formed in session 1) selects one script from Assignment 1, then writes a teaser script, creates a shot list, and films a simple 20-second teaser
Editing is not required during class; groups only need to combine clips into one unedited sequence and export it
The final edited version must be submitted no later than 2 days afterward
Students are recommended to use AI tools to enhance the quality of shot footage

AI Task Completion, Human Evaluation

Students are permitted to use AI for some or most elements of the task and demonstrate effective use of AI. They are expected to evaluate output irrespective of how it is attained, keep all prompts and output, and acknowledge and cite AI created content in their final submission.

- From session 25 to 30
- Each group (formed in session 1) reproduces and processes the audio for the teaser created in Assignment 2, applying the knowledge learned in class
Based on the idea chosen in Assignment 2, write a script, then shoot and edit it into a final media product.

Full AI

Students are expected to use AI creatively and collaboratively to complete the task and demonstrate effective use of AI. They are expected to evaluate output, keep all prompts and output, and acknowledge and cite AI created content in their final submission.

- From session 34 to 48

- Each group (formed in session 1) based on the idea which was chosen in Assignment 2, write a script then shooting and editing to a final media product which could be:

1. TVC/Promo

2. MV

3. Viral Clip

4. Mini Documentary

5. Short Movie

6. Others

Duration of the final product must not exceed 5 mins

Each group has to take turn show the final project and present how the project was operating in a presentation with no more than 7 slides

Presenting time should not exceed 7 mins

Q&A should not exceed 7 mins

Total time for each group should not exceed 20 mins

- Student must submit

(1) An AI report for AI usage with information about AI generated footages with specific prompts used.

(2) Final product

(3) Workfile (or screenshot working sequence)
